questions.problem:
In **ascending order**, the solutions to ${y}^{2}-y=0$ are $y=${{field-1}} and $y=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-y & =0 \\ y(y-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get

$$
y=0\,\text{or}\,y-1=0,
$$

which in turn gives

$$
y=0\,\text{or}\,y=1.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=0$ and $y=1.$

questions.problem:
In **ascending order**, the solutions to $\frac{2}{5}{z}^{2}=-2z$ are $z=${{field-1}} and $z=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{z}^{2} & =-2z \\ \frac{2}{5}{z}^{2}+2z & =0 \\ \frac{2}{5}z(z+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get

$$
\frac{2}{5}z=0\,\text{or}\,z+5=0,
$$

which in turn gives

$$
z=0\,\text{or}\,z=-5.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $z=-5$ and $z=0.$

questions.problem:
In **ascending order**, the solutions to $3{t}^{2}=\frac{t}{3}$ are $t=${{field-1}} and $t=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2} & =\frac{t}{3} \\ 3{t}^{2}-\frac{t}{3} & =0 \\ t(3t-\frac{1}{3}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get

$$
t=0\,\text{or}\,3t-\frac{1}{3}=0,
$$

which in turn gives

$$
t=0\,\text{or}\,t=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $t=0$ and $t=\frac{1}{9}.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we factor the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}+12n & =0 \\ n(n+12) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get 

$$
n=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad n+12=0,
$$

which in turn gives 

$$
n=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad n=-12.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $n=-12,0.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Solving When the Right-Hand Side Is Not Zero
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

$$
\eqalign{
	3p^2 &= 5p \[3pt]
	3p^2 - 5p &= 0 \[3pt]
	p(3p - 5) &= 0
}
$$

So, by the zero product rule, we have

$$
p=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad 3p-5=0,
$$

which in turn gives 

$$
p=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad p=\dfrac{5}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p=0,\dfrac{5}{3}.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Solving When Both Sides are Quadratic
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}+2x-2 & =8{x}^{2}-x-2 \\ 6{x}^{2}+2x-2-(8{x}^{2}-x-2) & =0 \\ 6{x}^{2}+2x-2-8{x}^{2}+x+2 & =0 \\ (6{x}^{2}-8{x}^{2})+(2x+x)+(-2+2) & =0 \\ -2{x}^{2}+3x+0 & =0 \\ -2{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ x(-2x+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, by the zero product rule, we have

$$
x=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad -2x + 3=0,
$$

which in turn gives 

$$
x=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=\dfrac{3}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=0,\dfrac{3}{2}.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To solve a two-term quadratic equation like $x^2 - 7x = 0$ where there is no constant term, we can factor out the variable and apply the zero-product rule.

Factoring out the variable, we have:

$$
\eqalign{
	x^2 - 7x &= 0 \
	x(x - 7) &= 0
}
$$

We apply the zero product rule to get 

$$
x=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x-7=0,
$$

which in turn gives 

$$
x=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=7.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=0,7.$

To check that these solutions are correct, we can substitute them back into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =0 & \, & \, & x & =7 \\  & ⇓ &  &  &  & ⇓ \\ {x}^{2}-7x & =0 &  &  & {x}^{2}-7x & =0 \\ {0}^{2}-7(0) & =0 &  &  & {7}^{2}-7(7) & =0 \\ 0-0 & =0 &  &  & 49-49 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓ &  &  & 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

**Warning:** It's tempting to solve the equation by dividing by $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-7x & =0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}-7x}{x} & =\frac{0}{x} \\ x-7 & =0 \\ x & =7\end{aligned}
$$

However, if we do that, we lose the solution $x=0.$ So, when solving equations, *never divide by a variable* because the variable could be zero, and division by zero is not allowed. Instead, try to factor the variable in the equation.
